records.benchmarkId: MAPLE independent same-indication randomized comparator and FOREST open-label persistence
records.benchmarkContext: MAPLE and SEQUOIA were separate blinded pivotal oHCM trials but had different comparators. FOREST long-term open-label follow-up is selected, not randomized durability confirmation.
records.observedResult: SEQUOIA NCT05186818 randomized placebo-adjusted peak VO2 +1.7 mL/kg/min at week 24. The independent MAPLE-HCM Phase 3 active-control trial found +2.3 mL/kg/min against metoprolol. FOREST-HCM observed in 296 oHCM trial completers median 51.6 weeks follow-up; at week 96 NYHA and KCCQ improved and LVOT gradient was reduced, supporting some on-treatment persistence.
records.uncertaintyReview: FOREST is not blinded and its parent-trial composition cannot be treated as SEQUOIA-only; cross-pivotal comparator differences prevent pooling and full subgroup interaction results are unavailable.
records.criticalRiskReview: Open-label responder selection and lack of independent long-term blinded replication limit strength of durability inference.
records.reviewerMethod: Mixed research grade, independently positive direction for same indication and long-term observational persistence, but uncertainty remains.

records.benchmarkId: SEQUOIA randomized oHCM precedent, a different comparator and clinical trial
records.benchmarkContext: Both independent randomized trials concern symptomatic obstructive HCM and aficamten, but MAPLE was against metoprolol and SEQUOIA against placebo. Evidence supports replicated direction not identical effect or long-term MAPLE-specific durability.
records.observedResult: MAPLE NCT05767346 randomized 88 aficamten versus 87 metoprolol with 24-week adjusted peak VO2 difference +2.3 mL/kg/min (95% CI +1.5 to +3.1, P<0.001). The separate SEQUOIA trial reported a 24-week placebo-adjusted +1.7 mL/kg/min, 95% CI +1.0 to +2.4.
records.uncertaintyReview: Positive short-term direction replicated with different controls, but 52-week MAPLE treatment durability, all subgroup interaction CIs, and comparative long-term cardiac safety require more evidence.
records.criticalRiskReview: Effect may be comparator-dependent; no cross-study equivalence or direct comparison with another myosin inhibitor can be inferred.
records.reviewerMethod: Mixed 50 research grade for replicated direction with incomplete MAPLE-specific long-term durability and subgroup evidence.

records.benchmarkId: FDA multiple-endpoint error control and missing-data review standards
records.benchmarkContext: Both Phase 3 studies are distinct blinded placebo-controlled trials reporting highly significant prespecified primary UAS7 contrasts, but sponsor toplines omit full statistical analysis plans, confidence intervals and missing-data sensitivity results.
records.observedResult: EMBARQ-CSU1 at week 12 published a -20.2 UAS7 LS mean change at 150 mg versus placebo change -10.7 with P<0.00001 for the between-group comparison. Complete UAS7=0 response was 42.4% versus 9.3%, P<0.00001. Sponsor reported both dose regimens met primary and key secondary endpoints in this and companion Phase 3 trials.
records.uncertaintyReview: Treatment differences are supported by nominal tests and standard errors, but no full endpoint-by-endpoint multiplicity hierarchy, primary-effect confidence interval or missingness sensitivity was supplied in the released summary.
records.criticalRiskReview: Strong sponsor P values are not a complete blinded SAP, and randomized safety/completer data after week 24 remain incompletely disclosed.
records.reviewerMethod: Mixed 50 research assessment for strong reported statistical signals with material unreviewed missingness and multiplicity details.

records.benchmarkId: 2024 ESC guideline context for ambulatory systolic blood-pressure improvement
records.benchmarkContext: ESC guidance estimates standard BP-drug office effect about 9/5 mmHg and ABPM effect about 5/3 mmHg. This is contextual cardiovascular relevance, not a GRACE-specific validated quality-of-life or Cushing MCID benchmark.
records.observedResult: GRACE NCT03697109 randomized-withdrawal hypertension responders: loss of BP control 11/21 (52%) on continued relacorilant vs 19/22 (86%) after placebo substitution, 34 percentage points favoring treatment. Ambulatory SBP adjusted between-arm difference -6.5 mmHg (95% CI -11.9 to -1.1; P=0.019) in evaluable paired subset.
records.uncertaintyReview: The cohort was selected for response during prior open-label treatment, so results do not establish population-wide patient benefit. Patient-reported physical function, hospitalization and survival improvement not demonstrated in these randomized data.
records.criticalRiskReview: Improved blood pressure is a health-relevant intermediate outcome, not direct proof of subjective function or survival for Cushing patients.
records.reviewerMethod: Mixed clinical benefit assessment for patient-relevant hypertension control among selected responders and incomplete direct PRO results.

records.benchmarkId: FDA multiple-endpoint statistical control context and the GRACE protocol change
records.benchmarkContext: GRACE original protocol had two co-primary efficacy endpoints and later specified hypertension-loss primary. FDA expects prospective protection against multiplicity and appropriate missing-data sensitivity. Primary estimates and analyses are concordant but a fully prospective protocol-change audit has not been performed.
records.observedResult: GRACE NCT03697109 hypertension loss primary ITT OR 0.17, 95% CI 0.04 to 0.77, P=0.022 (11/21 vs 19/22). Modified ITT 9/19 vs 15/18 (P=0.029), per-protocol 7/15 vs 15/18 (P=0.032). Trial treated missing week-12 data as loss of response; only 62 total subjects randomized after open-label enrichment.
records.uncertaintyReview: Primary analysis and two sensitivity subsets remain conventionally significant, but small n, original co-primary endpoint amendment, and selected study population limit certainty.
records.criticalRiskReview: Changes to prespecified endpoints can affect confirmatory inference; responder-enriched withdrawal may magnify treatment difference compared to an all-randomized prospective trial.
records.reviewerMethod: Mixed 50 for positive primary CI and sensitivity checks with significant multiplicity and selection questions.

records.benchmarkId: Independent GRADIENT same-drug trial in adrenal-only etiology, not a successful direct GRACE replication
records.benchmarkContext: GRACE showed BP responder maintenance during 12-week double-blind withdrawal after 22 weeks of open-label treatment. GRADIENT was a separate blinded study of relacorilant in adrenal hypercortisolism with a nonsignificant placebo-adjusted SBP primary, limiting the replication claim.
records.observedResult: In GRACE, 11/21 continued relacorilant vs 19/22 placebo-substituted patients lost BP control by week 12, showing a sustained on-treatment contrast in selected patients. Independent GRADIENT NCT04308590 had relacorilant SBP reduction -6.6 versus -2.1 mmHg placebo but the between-group primary comparison was nonsignificant.
records.uncertaintyReview: The open-label treatment period and short randomized-withdrawal window do not establish long-term randomized maintenance in all hypercortisolism etiologies. Different etiology and trial design limit direct cross-study reproducibility.
records.criticalRiskReview: The placebo-substitution design enriches responders, and GRADIENT primary miss is a meaningful counterexample rather than positive independent replication.
records.reviewerMethod: Mixed 50 for observable within-GRACE maintenance offset by lack of unequivocal same-population independent replication.

records.benchmarkId: Cross-trial relacorilant tolerability reports, different Cushing etiology and not a randomized peer-drug comparison
records.benchmarkContext: GRACE published arm-level withdrawal AEs in 30 relacorilant vs 32 placebo participants; GRADIENT sponsor reports consistent qualitative tolerability. Neither study directly compares against mifepristone or steroidogenesis inhibitors, and rare-event confidence is limited.
records.observedResult: GRACE randomized-withdrawal safety: back pain 5/30 versus 6/32, headache 3/30 versus 4/32, acne 3/30 versus 0, bursitis 3/30 versus 0, and withdrawal discontinuation 5/30 versus 5/32. No hypokalemia, adrenal insufficiency, endometrial hypertrophy bleeding, or drug-induced QT prolongation observed in the trial.
records.uncertaintyReview: Earlier GRACE open-label stage had 57/152 discontinuations for multiple reasons including AEs and withdrawal. A small selected 12-week randomized population does not establish rare or long-term safety or peer drug superiority.
records.criticalRiskReview: Do not interpret absence of observed endocrine signal as zero future risk or as a controlled safety superiority claim against FDA-approved drugs.
records.reviewerMethod: Mixed 50 for documented and mostly comparable common AEs during randomized withdrawal, limited long-term and peer comparator evidence.

records.indication: hypercortisolism caused by cortisol-secreting adrenal adenomas or hyperplasia
records.benchmarkId: 2024 ESC BP reduction clinical context; the study's prespecified placebo-adjusted superiority test is decisive
records.benchmarkContext: Within-arm ABPM improvement can be meaningful, but the prespecified randomized between-group systolic BP endpoint is the success criterion, not the within-treated-arm P value. ESC guidance contextualizes BP magnitude but is not the trial regulatory threshold.
records.observedResult: GRADIENT NCT04308590 randomized 137 adults for 22 weeks. Mean ABPM systolic BP reduced 6.6 mmHg with relacorilant (within-arm P=0.012) and 2.1 mmHg with placebo (within-arm nonsignificant). Issuer explicitly states the primary placebo-adjusted between-arm SBP comparison was NOT statistically significant.
records.uncertaintyReview: Full between-arm primary confidence interval and trial SAP were not disclosed; known inferential primary miss remains source documented, while exact possible effect sizes are uncertain.
records.criticalRiskReview: Within-arm significance cannot substitute for a randomized between-arm success; nominally positive secondary outcomes do not overturn prespecified primary failure.
records.reviewerMethod: Below-benchmark clinical efficacy score for known missed between-arm primary endpoint, not a zero or an FDA outcome prediction.

records.indication: hypercortisolism caused by cortisol-secreting adrenal adenomas or hyperplasia
records.benchmarkId: ESC BP medical relevance as contextual comparator; no quality-of-life or hard cardiovascular outcome evidence
records.benchmarkContext: GRADIENT's prespecified between-group SBP primary was nonsignificant, while metabolic and weight secondary comparisons were reported with favorable nominal effects. These surrogate outcomes are potentially patient-important but do not establish patient-reported wellbeing or survival.
records.observedResult: GRADIENT NCT04308590 showed placebo-adjusted fasting glucose change -22.2 mg/dL (P=0.002), oral glucose tolerance AUC -2.6 h*mmol/L (P=0.046), HbA1c -0.3 percentage point (P=0.019) and body weight -3.9 kg (P=0.0001). Five placebo vs one treated patients needed antihypertensive rescue; prespecified SBP primary comparison was nonsignificant.
records.uncertaintyReview: Nominal secondary P values may not be familywise significant after a failed primary; no independently verified patient QoL or hard health outcome is established.
records.criticalRiskReview: Potential clinical importance is offset by failed primary and reliance on surrogate rather than directly experienced patient benefit.
records.reviewerMethod: Mixed 50 for positive reported metabolic patient-relevant measurements counterbalanced by negative hypertension primary and missing QoL evidence.

records.indication: hypercortisolism caused by cortisol-secreting adrenal adenomas or hyperplasia
records.benchmarkId: FDA multiplicity guidance gives prespecified primary testing precedence over nominal secondary subgroup significance
records.benchmarkContext: A prespecified placebo-adjusted primary failing significance cannot be replaced by within-arm favorable change or unadjusted positives in several secondary endpoints. Source publication lacks full SAP and imputation analyses.
records.observedResult: GRADIENT NCT04308590 issuer stated prespecified between-group SBP primary was not statistically significant, even though relacorilant within-arm change was -6.6 mmHg (P=0.012). Nominal placebo-adjusted fasting glucose P=0.002 and body-weight P=0.0001 were favorable but are secondary.
records.uncertaintyReview: Missing full primary confidence interval, dropout-adjusted sensitivity and multiplicity hierarchy mean secondary robustness is not settled; known primary miss is an adverse inferential fact rather than an unknown.
records.criticalRiskReview: Post-hoc replacement of a failed primary with secondary outcomes would inflate false-positive conclusions and overstate statistical certainty.
records.reviewerMethod: Below-benchmark 25 for missed confirmatory primary, distinct from missing complete SAP details and not a FDA rejection probability.

records.drug: LB-102 (100 mg tablet) | LB-102 (50 mg tablet)
records.benchmarkId: Sponsor documented steady-state D2/D3 receptor engagement and exploratory 100mg cohort versus blinded 50mg and 75mg
records.benchmarkContext: LB-102 50mg human PET 70% receptor occupancy and 100mg >80% occupancy, but larger exposure is not a validated efficacy threshold and Phase2 was only four weeks.
records.observedResult: NOVA-1 NCT06179108 in 359 adults: placebo PANSS -9.3, LB-102 50mg -14.3 (P<0.001), 75mg -14.0 (P=0.002), and 100mg -16.1 (nominal P=0.002; exploratory n=36). Clinical receptor occupancy at 50mg near 70%, at 100mg over 80%; 50/75 results were not monotonic and 100mg small.
records.uncertaintyReview: Dose receptor activity is human demonstrated but no unequivocal monotonic 50-to-75mg efficacy separation; 100mg estimate imprecise. Published evidence is Phase2, not efficacy in unreported Phase3 NOVA-2.
records.criticalRiskReview: High prolactin and weight increases in phase2 plus limited n=36 at 100mg could impair higher dose tolerability, and human target engagement does not guarantee later readout success.
records.reviewerMethod: Mixed 50 for demonstrated human target engagement and some dose response with discordant interim dose efficacy and clinical safety uncertainty.

records.drug: LB-102 (100 mg tablet) | LB-102 (50 mg tablet)
records.benchmarkId: Explicit alternate efficacy explanations from randomized four-week PANSS study and pivotal ongoing stage
records.benchmarkContext: A placebo-controlled short-term inpatient symptomatic PANSS improvement is an informative biological/clinical signal but not an out-of-sample proof. Small exploratory 100mg cohort and 80% male trial population inform generalization.
records.observedResult: NOVA-1 Phase2 NCT06179108 formal 50mg and 75mg placebo-adjusted PANSS reductions were significant at four weeks with different Hedges g values 0.61 and 0.41. 100mg exploratory dose n=36 showed nominal stronger change. 50mg and 75mg effects were similar rather than dose-ordered; secondary patient benefits and negative symptoms have multiplicity and pseudospecificity caveats.
records.uncertaintyReview: Open active Phase3 NCT07363577 has no readout. The high placebo response, short inpatient period, 100mg sample imbalance, secondary multiplicity and efficacy safety tradeoff remain possible contrary explanations for Phase3 failure.
records.criticalRiskReview: Reported frequent prolactin elevation and weight gain weaken any claim of universal safety advantage and must not be ignored in the prospective readout case.
records.reviewerMethod: Mixed 50: source-backed positive Phase2 but material identified counterhypotheses remain; cannot claim Phase3 success.

records.benchmarkId: Earlier randomized NAL ER dose-ranging CORAL and previous randomized IPF cough crossover
records.benchmarkContext: Both the 2026 165-person randomized dose-ranging study and prior small randomized crossover study measured objective cough frequency versus placebo; endpoint measures and exposure periods differ and do not establish Phase3 durability.
records.observedResult: Phase2b CORAL NCT05964335 randomized 165 IPF cough participants: placebo-adjusted relative objective 24-hour cough frequency reductions at week6 were 30.9% at 27mg twice daily (P<0.01), 36.5% at 54mg (P<0.001), and 43.3% at 108mg (P<0.001). Earlier 41-person blinded crossover NCT04030026 reported 52.5-point placebo-adjusted daytime cough-frequency reduction after 21 days.
records.uncertaintyReview: Three coherent doses and repeat objective within-disease effects support human dose/exposure response, but only six-week parallel and three-week crossover observations exist; phase3 NCT07671911 remains recruiting.
records.criticalRiskReview: Opioid-mediated adverse effects nausea, vomiting, constipation and dizziness, plus up-titration tolerability, could limit chronic dose adoption and compromise blinding.
records.reviewerMethod: Above-benchmark 75 for replicated objective human pharmacodynamic cough suppression and consistent graded dose response, with phase3 durability unknown.

records.benchmarkId: Randomized comparison against placebo and previously published crossover evidence under distinct design
records.benchmarkContext: Multiple controlled studies support an objective cough-suppression signal, while adverse-event-mediated unblinding, short exposure, placebo response and IPF selection are possible explanations for inflated response or impaired generalization.
records.observedResult: CORAL NCT05964335 165 participants demonstrated relative placebo-adjusted cough reductions of about 31%-43% across three NAL ER doses at six weeks, with patient-reported cough subscale change at 27mg nonsignificant (P=0.14) despite objective efficacy, versus significant at 54/108mg; TEAE discontinuations 5.6% combined NAL ER versus 5.0% placebo.
records.uncertaintyReview: Objective efficacy is replicated in a much smaller 2023 crossover cohort, but longer Phase3 OCEAN-1 and OCEAN-2 outcomes, daily functioning, tolerability and dropout effects are unknown.
records.criticalRiskReview: Dose-limiting nausea/dizziness and discrepancy at the lowest-dose patient report could undermine practical patient benefit despite objective cough changes.
records.reviewerMethod: Mixed 50 for positive randomized objective cough evidence with meaningful safety and patient-report contradictions that can alter Phase3 readout.

records.benchmarkId: Independent placebo-controlled phase2 ARGO ACR50 comparator benchmark, not a Phase3 IZAR-1 comparator
records.benchmarkContext: ARGO Phase2 sonelokimab 60mg-with-induction ACR50 week12 46.3% versus placebo 20.0% (OR 3.6, CI 1.3-9.9). IZAR-1 sponsor explicitly withheld week16 placebo arm and comparative contrasts while continuing blinding through week52.
records.observedResult: IZAR-1 NCT06641076 sponsor announced ACR50 primary endpoint met at week16, with 42.1% receiving sonelokimab 60mg with induction attaining ACR50. Additional active-arm ACR20 66.5% and PASI90 61% were reported. The actual phase3 placebo ACR50 percentage, effect CI and exact between-arm P value were not disclosed.
records.uncertaintyReview: The positive top-line conclusion is accepted at face value, but effect magnitude relative to placebo is unknown. ARGO 2025 data are historical context only and cannot be transferred to the blinded Phase3 placebo arm.
records.criticalRiskReview: No phase3 comparative CI or full treatment arm data; cannot characterize efficacy as unequivocally superior or FDA-sufficient.
records.reviewerMethod: Research-only mixed 50 for sponsor-confirmed positive pivotal clinical outcome with material masked placebo effect; not an imputed comparison.

records.benchmarkId: Within-treatment clinical function score changes with Phase2 multidomain patient outcome context
records.benchmarkContext: HAQ-DI and SF-36 PCS are validated function and quality-of-life instruments, but the sponsor release does not provide phase3 blinded placebo-group functional changes or between-group confidence intervals.
records.observedResult: IZAR-1 NCT06641076 60mg with induction reported week16 HAQ-DI mean change -0.427 and SF-36 PCS mean change +6.54, with ACR20 66.5%, MDA 41.2%, and skin PASI90 61%. Sponsor described all endpoints as met and significant; raw placebo responses and adjusted differences are intentionally undisclosed.
records.uncertaintyReview: Patient-functional observations are encouraging and clinically relevant, but the exact incremental benefit versus placebo cannot be established from the blinded interim release, and long-term PRO durability to week52 is not disclosed.
records.criticalRiskReview: Unblinded dose-arm averages can reflect regression to mean and placebo; this is a provisional source-report rating, not proof of comparative clinical superiority.
records.reviewerMethod: Mixed 50 for reported functional improvement and multidomain response with no quantitative comparator to establish effect magnitude.

records.benchmarkId: ARGO 2025 independent earlier phase2 same-indication and dose clinical trial, not pivotal Phase3 replication
records.benchmarkContext: The peer-reviewed 2025 Phase2 ARGO trial (NCT05640245) provides a separate randomized PsA effect signal with sonelokimab but cannot establish durability of the currently blinded 2026 Phase3 IZAR-1 at week52.
records.observedResult: ARGO Phase2 reported week12 ACR50 46.3% at 60mg with induction versus placebo 20.0% (P<0.05), and week24 ACR50 rates about 58%-61% on-treatment. IZAR-1 Phase3 NCT06641076 reported 42.1% on-treatment ACR50 at week16 and sponsor stated primary and secondary endpoints were met.
records.uncertaintyReview: Two randomized studies support the direction of clinical response across phases, but their doses, populations, time points and comparator visibility differ. IZAR-1 remains blinded through 52-week readout, so no phase3 durability or subgroup interactions can be independently assessed.
records.criticalRiskReview: Cross-phase comparison cannot substitute for a second independent complete placebo-controlled pivotal study, and no phase3 long-term relapse data are yet available.
records.reviewerMethod: Mixed 50 for qualitative signal replication across Phase2 and Phase3 with unavailable Phase3 longer-term durability.

records.benchmarkId: Separate 2024 GRACE relacorilant trial in endogenous hypercortisolism but different etiology and randomized withdrawal design

GRACE NCT03697109 documented maintenance of hypertension control during 12-week blinded withdrawal in patients previously responding.
records.uncertaintyReview: GRADIENT 22-week primary is negative, and no subsequent independent adrenal-only confirmation or longer blinded durability has been disclosed, but other relacorilant hypercortisolism subgroup signals exist.

records.reviewerMethod: Mixed 50 for heterogeneous same-drug clinical observations; failed GRADIENT primary and absent same-etiology replicated durability are major limitations.

records.indication: hypercortisolism caused by cortisol-secreting adrenal adenomas or hyperplasia
records.benchmarkId: Direct GRADIENT placebo safety arm; GRACE is same-molecule distinct-population context only
records.benchmarkContext: The direct adverse-event comparison is within GRADIENT NCT04308590: relacorilant n=68 versus placebo n=69, not a cross-trial efficacy or safety comparison. The linked GRACE source concerns another hypercortisolism population and cannot be pooled or treated as an approved medical peer comparator.
records.observedResult: ClinicalTrials.gov posted GRADIENT NCT04308590 results reported treatment-emergent adverse events through week 26 in 67 of 68 relacorilant patients (98.5%) versus 60 of 69 placebo patients (87.0%). Serious-adverse-event term tables include dyspnoea 2/68 versus 0/69 and acute myocardial infarction 1/68 versus 1/69; these counts are term-level and cannot be summed as unique patients with serious events.
records.uncertaintyReview: The higher frequency of any TEAE on active treatment is recorded, but treatment causality cannot be established from aggregate event counts. The published source lacks an indication-matched active-treatment peer head-to-head, full per-patient attribution and sufficiently long follow-up to exclude rare harms.
records.criticalRiskReview: Cardiovascular and infection or tumor-related events require case-by-case adjudication rather than automatic attribution; earlier comparisons are not proof of long-term safety superiority. This is not an FDA safety determination.
records.reviewerMethod: Source-accepted primary registry arm-level data graded mixed 50 for substantial adverse-event burden and treatment-arm imbalance with limited attribution and matched-peer evidence; historical research only.

records.reviewerMethod: Source-accepted clinical efficacy research grade 75: strong prespecified placebo-controlled opioid abstinence difference; not an FDA forecast.
